items.title: Bob Cranshaw interviewed by Michael Woods, New York City, New York, October 18, 1995
items.q: I feel like I’m a Milt Hinton clone in a way... I wanted to be Milt Hinton. I wanted to be this. The next Milt Hinton was my dream. I just wanted to be like he was.

ctx.x: a guy’s taking a solo and he’s out there and he’s saying something abstract and he wants to come back down home, he’ll play that blues scale.

Because it’s so much, not only are the changes just right, but the feeling of the music, you know. I mean Joe, I grew up on Joe Williams. I mean I can say as a young guy, I was young at that time and it was just right for me. Because Joe’s stuff was very structured. But he was such a professional. We would get on the stage and we were swinging. I mean the music felt so good. Every night it was just very consistent. And the trio was Junior Mance and Mickey Roker. And we had a good time with each other but it was a…

items.title: Milt Hinton interviewed by Joe Williams, Majesty of the Seas, May 31, 1995
items.q: I remember Bob Cranshaw looking over my shoulder... observing what is required of him... And one day you were around Cranshaw... Cran says, 'Come on over here and let me show you.'

ctx.x: Yeah, we came in to — he was the only one of the trio that came in to one of the record dates because I always was fortunate enough to get you, Osie Johnson, and Hank Jones, and with Jimmy Jones and I would wait ‘til we could get you, until you were available to have our record dates.
I remember Bob Cranshaw looking over my shoulder, I’ve got pictures of him looking over my shoulder observing what is required of him. Now he’s in the recording studio.
That’s true. But you know the thing about that that was so beautiful, you were doing the, with Bobby Rosengarden, you were doing the television show. What’s the boy’s name?
